\section[el campeonato]{el campeonato — the championship}

\label{lesson:ES-C498-campeonato}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to look after, then the Spanish for friendship.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el campeonato}
\textbf{el campeonato} — \textquotedblleft{}the championship\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ganamos el campeonato de baloncesto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We won the basketball championship.}
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[el deportista]{el deportista — the sportsperson, the athlete}

\label{lesson:ES-C498-deportista}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for friendship, then the Spanish for the championship.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el deportista}
\textbf{el deportista} — \textquotedblleft{}the sportsperson, the athlete\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Es una deportista muy conocida.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She is a very well-known athlete.}
\end{quote}

The same form for a woman: \emph{la deportista}.

\section[competir]{competir — to compete}

\label{lesson:ES-C498-competir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the championship, then the Spanish for the sportsperson.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: competir}
\textbf{competir} — \textquotedblleft{}to compete\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Compite en los cien metros.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He competes in the hundred metres.}
\end{quote}

The e breaks into i: \emph{compito}.

\section[montar]{montar — to ride; to set up}

\label{lesson:ES-C498-montar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the sportsperson, then the Spanish for to compete.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: montar}
\textbf{montar} — \textquotedblleft{}to ride; to set up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Monto en bici los domingos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I ride my bike on Sundays.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Montar a caballo} — to ride a horse. In much of Latin America people say \emph{andar en bici}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}
